lesson.title: Synthetic fixture: predict rotating field speed

blocks.title: What you will work through
blocks.text: Explain the rule in your own words, then check an authored calculation.

blocks.title: Check the source rule

citations.quote: Synchronous field speed equals 120 times frequency in hertz divided by the total number of poles.

blocks.text: Synchronous field speed equals 120 times frequency in hertz divided by the total number of poles.

blocks.title: An authored calculation

citations.quote: Synchronous field speed equals 120 times frequency in hertz divided by the total number of poles.

blocks.text: With authored inputs 50 Hz and four poles: 120 × 50 ÷ 4 = 1,500 rpm. This is calculated synchronous field speed.

blocks.title: Predict before changing a value

citations.quote: Synchronous field speed equals 120 times frequency in hertz divided by the total number of poles.

blocks.prompt: Predict field speed for 50 Hz and six poles, then check the local calculator when integrated.

blocks.title: Check your reasoning

citations.quote: Synchronous field speed equals 120 times frequency in hertz divided by the total number of poles.

blocks.prompt: Using the rule with authored inputs 50 Hz and four poles, which result is the synchronous field speed?

blocks.title: Explain the limit
blocks.text: Explain why a calculated rotating-field value should not be presented as measured equipment behaviour.
